title: Circuit symbols card
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 32 (Circuit symbols card (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 32: Electric circuits and symbols. To understand what an electric current is and how a complete circuit lets it flow

questions.q: Draw a circuit: one cell, one lamp, one closed switch.
questions.a: Rectangle loop with the cell, lamp and closed switch symbols
questions.model: Start with the cell symbol (long line, short line). Draw a wire round as a rectangle. Add the lamp (circle with a cross) on one side and the closed switch on another.

questions.q: Why does opening a switch turn off the lamp?
questions.a: It makes a gap so the circuit is not complete; no current flows
Two or more cells joined together

questions.q: Build three circuits in the simulator and draw each with symbols: (a) one cell, one lamp; (b) add a switch; (c) two lamps in a line. Say whether each lamp lights.
questions.a: All lamps light when the switch is closed; diagrams with correct symbols and square corners
questions.model: Teacher builds circuit (a) in the simulator on screen and draws it: cell, wire, lamp, back to the cell.

questions.q: Explain why a torch with one cell the wrong way round does not work.
questions.a: The cells push against each other, so there is little or no current.

questions.q: A string of lamps all go out when one breaks. What does that tell you about the circuit?
questions.a: They are in series: one break opens the only path.

questions.q: Big question: why might a torch not switch on?
questions.a: The circuit is incomplete: flat cell, broken lamp, gap, or cell the wrong way.
